snippet.title: jio vs starlink
snippet.description:
JIO vs STARLINK: Elon Musk's Battle for India's Internet | Nikhil Kamath
Could Elon Musk's Starlink challenge Reliance Jio in India?
Elon Musk explains to Nikhil Kamath why SpaceX wants to bring Starlink to India and how satellite internet could change connectivity, particularly in rural areas.
Traditional telecom networks rely on infrastructure such as fibre-optic cables and cellular towers. Building these networks in remote locations can be expensive. Starlink takes a different approach by using satellites to deliver internet connectivity.
That creates an interesting contrast in India: Jio's established mobile network versus Starlink's satellite-based technology.
The debate has become even more heated amid Musk's public comments about Mukesh Ambani's influence and the process for Starlink's entry into India.
But this isn't simply a question of which company is bigger. It's about whether satellite internet can expand access, create new competition, and serve places that existing infrastructure doesn't reach as effectively.
Will Starlink become a serious challenger in India, or will Jio continue to dominate the internet market?

snippet.description:
Dubai Has A Service Where You Can Rent Friends
What if you could pay someone to pretend to be your friend?
In this clip from the WTF Podcast, Omar Al Olama tells Nikhil Kamath about an unusual video he discovered on Instagram: a service in Dubai that allows people to rent friends for social activities.
Want someone to run with you in the Dubai Marathon? You can pay for it.
Want to play paddle tennis but don't have enough friends to join? You can rent three people to play alongside you.
According to Omar, these rented friends may even act as if they already know you, praise your performance, and deliberately lose so you can win.
It's a strange concept that raises a bigger question about friendship, loneliness, and the growing business of selling social experiences.
Would you ever pay someone to act like your friend, or is that taking things too far?
